These include intake with no cap; the ordered 1-to-6 spill with cascade and stage 6 to ground; hysteresis using >= U and <= D with the state held in between, and at most one change per cycle; the snapshot release using floor(/4) for CLEAR and floor(/2) for ASSERTED, sent to n-1, with stage 1 to ground and no cap; over-capacity persisting into the next spill or into the end figures in cycle 5; the strictly-greater-than-38 halving with the removed charge to ground; and the balance check. domainPull: The pull was strongest at the 'return diode' and the 'breaker'. A real diode conducts only toward lower potential, yet the document sends ASSERTED discharge to stage n-1 unconditionally, even into a stage already over its rating. A real breaker opens the circuit instead of halving every charge. A further pull was letting a stage sit above its rated charge after feedback, which a real breakdown shunt would clamp continuously. Nobody fell for any of these, and all three operators explicitly kept the cycle 5 over-rated stages 2 (10>8) and 4 (7>6).
